decisive_items: SARS-CoV-2 antigen test positive (>5000 pg/mL) from oropharyngeal swab
Histology showed diffuse contraction band necrosis with several lymphocytes in cardiac muscle
response.rationale: SARS-CoV-2 infection plus myocardial inflammation/necrosis, elevated cardiac markers, and ST elevation with no coronary stenosis point to COVID-19-associated myocarditis rather than ACS or a primary thrombotic microangiopathy.

rejected.why: Thrombocytopenia and platelet aggregation in cardiac microvessels are present, but without systemic TMA features such as hemolysis, schistocytes, or renal/neurologic involvement; this is more likely secondary microvascular thrombosis in COVID-19.
COVID-19-related myocardial injury is too broad; the lymphocytic infiltration and myocyte necrosis support myocarditis specifically.
Myocarditis is compatible, but omits the confirmed COVID-19 etiology, making it less specific than R2.
ST elevation and elevated troponin mimic ACS, but the absence of coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis and the viral/inflammatory context make ACS unlikely.
Pulmonary infiltrates and heavy lungs are present, but the dominant clinical and autopsy findings are cardiac; ARDS is not the primary diagnosis.
